name: Jeb Thomas-Mitchell
bio: I am an HCI/AI MSc student under Professor Fanny Chevalier at the University of Toronto. I also completed my BSc in Computer Science at the University of Toronto with a focus on artificial intelligence.

My research focuses on understanding and enhancing human-AI creative collaborations through novel interface and interaction designs, with particular emphasis on protecting users' agency, ownership, and trust in AI-assisted creative work.

news.text: Presented our paper at CHI '26 in Barcelona: “Where Do I ‘Add the Egg’?”
Took part in the Herding CATS workshop at CHI '26 with our position paper: Bridging Workspace Awareness and Creative Activity Traces
Presented our paper at CSCW '25 in Bergen: Co-writing with AI, on Human Terms.

blurb: As a graduate student, I have been involved in teaching and TA work across several courses in computer science and HCI at the University of Toronto. My philosophy centres on helping students build their self-efficacy and creativity through a positive and inclusive environment.
If you’re a UofT student with questions about grad school or HCI research, feel free to reach out.
